corrections.caveats: First-party numbers; CPU model not stated. The headline 19-30x is for the native binary against the dart2js JS CLI, not WebAssembly; the wasm figure in a same-run table is 610 ms vs 2268 ms. The README's wasm-vs-dart comparison is cross-run (wasm refreshed 2026-06-13, dart-sass forms from an earlier full run at 1.100.0), and run_bench.sh does not time the wasm build at all. bench/three_way.md predates the allocation-reduction rounds by the README's own note. In the one-entry-point Linux x86_64 run (2026-10-02) the npm path is slower than dart-sass: 38.3 ms through node_modules/.bin/sasso vs 20.7 ms for dart-sass (the binary takes 4.3 ms). Category fit is loose: a Rust SCSS compiler that ships a wasm build, not a wasm-targeting language. Not a brand-new repo: crates.io crate created 2026-06-06, 1,557 commits; 7 stars.

notes: Numbers in the record match the README. Confirm at C; shortcomings: no CPU model, wasm timings outside the public harness and cross-run against dart-sass, npm CLI slower than dart-sass on a single entry point, loose fit for assemblyscript-and-wasm-langs (orchestrator may want a category override).
